title_en: Li Jincheng and Four Others — Speculation and Profiteering and Bribery Case
keywords_en: criminal; speculation and profiteering; bribery; first instance; Shanghai; state organ; Criminal Law; determination of speculation and profiteering; determination of bribery; distinction between unit crime and individual crime; reselling imported video recorders; reselling imported radio cassette recorders; illegal operation of smuggled video tapes; reselling motorcycles; speculating in woolen blankets; accepting bribes; fraud
full_text_en:
Li Jincheng et al. — case of speculation and bribery

Defendant: Li Jincheng, male, 57 years old, former Deputy Director of the Putuo Branch of the Shanghai Public Security Bureau, in charge of the Shanghai Huayi Comprehensive Trade Center. Arrested on November 2, 1985.

Defendant: Pan Jialin, male, 53 years old, former Section Chief of the Public Order Section of the Putuo Branch of the Shanghai Public Security Bureau, General Manager of the Shanghai Huayi Comprehensive Trade Center. Arrested on August 21, 1985.

Defendant: Chen Kunxing, male, 44 years old, former Deputy Director of the Anti-Smuggling Division and Captain of the Anti-Smuggling Team of Shanghai Customs, Deputy General Manager of the Shanghai Huayi Comprehensive Trade Center. Arrested on August 22, 1985.

Defendant: Tao Zhonglin, male, 29 years old, former cadre of the Public Order Section of the Putuo Branch of the Shanghai Public Security Bureau, Deputy General Manager of the Shanghai Huayi Comprehensive Trade Center. Arrested on July 29, 1985.

Defendant: Wang Hengming, male, 35 years old, former Deputy General Manager and Director of the Business Department of the Shanghai Huayi Comprehensive Trade Center (employed). From 1970 to 1983, he was dealt with six times by public security and prosecutorial authorities for offenses including illegal border crossing, fraud, gambling, and private sale of smuggled goods. Arrested on June 15, 1985.

Shanghai Huayi Comprehensive Trade Center (hereinafter referred to as "Huayi") was a collectively-owned enterprise jointly operated by the Putuo Branch of the Shanghai Public Security Bureau and Shanghai Customs. It was approved for business by the Putuo District Administration for Industry and Commerce of Shanghai on July 10, 1984, with a permitted business scope including general department store items, household appliances, food, cigarettes and groceries, and photo developing. It was composed of eight persons each transferred from the Putuo Branch and Shanghai Customs, and five employed idle persons from society. From July 1984 to January 1985, during the operation of "Huayi," the defendants Li Jincheng, Pan Jialin, Chen Kunxing, Tao Zhonglin, and Wang Hengming engaged in speculation (buying long and selling short, profiteering), selling goods not freely tradable under state regulations, with an illegal turnover of over RMB 2,273,000 and illegal profits of over RMB 268,000. During this period, Pan Jialin, Chen Kunxing, Tao Zhonglin, and Wang Hengming also accepted bribes. The specific criminal facts are as follows:

1. In violation of relevant state regulations, they sold 35 imported video recorders and two sets of video equipment; and sold 570 imported cassette recorders.

On August 25, 1984, with the consent of Pan Jialin and Li Jincheng, Tao Zhonglin, in the name of "Huayi," signed a contract with the Shanghai No. 9 Department Store (hereinafter "City No. 9 Store") for the supply of 100 imported Panasonic video recorders. On August 27, Pan Jialin and Tao Zhonglin went to Guangzhou on official business. Upon learning that Wang Hengming had used RMB 5,500 from case handling funds to buy one Panasonic video recorder from a target of investigation, Zhang X, Pan proposed using case handling funds to purchase goods, and Tao suggested buying video recorders. Subsequently, Pan, Tao, and Wang used case handling funds to buy eight Panasonic video recorders at RMB 7,700 each through the Guangzhou Wenda Commercial Firm from the Xihao Market of the Guangzhou Nanfang Department Store, paying a total of RMB 61,600. On September 2 of the same year, fearing "trouble" during transportation of these video recorders, Pan Jialin agreed to Tao Zhonglin's suggestion to alter the Putuo Branch's search warrant and seizure list; and at the Guangzhou Railway Station inspection, agreed to Tao Zhonglin and Wang Hengming presenting these documents. The three persons, by pretending that the nine video recorders were seized smuggled goods, deceived the railway police and transported them to Shanghai. Thereafter, Tao handled the resale of the nine video recorders at a markup to the City No. 9 Store. The illegal turnover was RMB 76,448, and illegal profits were RMB 9,348.

In September 1984, Tao Zhonglin, in the name of "Huayi," signed a contract with the City No. 9 Store for the sale of 10 Ai Lang brand video recorders, and received advance payment of RMB 88,000. Subsequently, Wang Hengming in Guangzhou purchased one Ai Lang brand video recorder from Chen XX, an agent of the Lianshan County Agriculture, Industry and Commerce United Corporation of Guangdong Province, for RMB 7,000, and also demanded one box of obscene videotape. After returning to Shanghai, Wang reported to the Putuo Branch that Chen XX was smuggling video recorders. On October 2 of the same year, Wang Hengming and Tao Zhonglin went to Guangzhou to handle the Chen XX smuggling case. On October 6, Li Jincheng, Chen Kunxing, and Pan Jialin went to Guangzhou together on official business and met with Wang and Tao, who had arrived earlier. They agreed that Tao would borrow a transfer check from the Guangzhou Wenda Commercial Firm (deliberately missing a seal on the check to prevent payment), take 25 video recorders from Chen XX, and then detain Chen. On October 8, despite Chen XX's defense that the video recorders were assembled in Zhuhai from imports and not smuggled goods, Li Jincheng, Pan Jialin, and Chen Kunxing, without investigation, decided to have Chen escorted back to Shanghai. At the same time, the 25 video recorders were handed over to the Guangzhou Wenda Commercial Firm, disguised as small general cargo and shipped to Shanghai. In mid-November of the same year, after investigation by the Putuo Branch, Li, Pan, and others already knew that these video recorders were not smuggled goods but still continued to detain Chen XX. Subsequently, Pan, in his capacity as Section Chief of the Public Security Bureau, directly negotiated with the original owner, the Zhuhai Hotel Mall, and purchased all of them at a unit price of RMB 4,700. "Huayi" sold 10 of them to the City No. 9 Store at a unit price of RMB 8,800. Thereafter, the remaining 15 were sold respectively to the Pacific Economic and Technical Information Center and Shanghai Customs at unit prices of RMB 8,000 and RMB 7,500. The illegal turnover was RMB 206,700, and illegal profits were RMB 82,200.

In October of the same year, Tao Zhonglin conspired with Pan Jialin to provide the City No. 9 Store with a blank "Huayi" purchase and sales contract form and bank account, to purchase two sets of Sony brand video equipment from the Zhongshan City Commercial Joint Trade Center of Guangdong Province, which were shipped to Shanghai by Liu XX of the Guangzhou Wenda Commercial Firm disguised as small general cargo. The illegal turnover was RMB 390,600. "Huayi," under the guise of collecting management fees, illegally profited RMB 18,600 from this.

In December 1984, with the consent of Li Jincheng and Pan Jialin, Wang Hengming purchased 70 imported Sharp brand cassette recorders from the Guangzhou Fangcun Labor Service Company (hereinafter "Fangcun Company") at a price of RMB 106,000, and sold 500 Sony brand cassette recorders on consignment for the Fangcun Company, valued at RMB 175,000. Of these, 65 Sharp cassette recorders and 221 Sony cassette recorders were resold by "Huayi" at a markup to the City No. 9 Store and other units. The illegal turnover was RMB 294,546, and illegal profits were RMB 13,546.

2. In violation of relevant state regulations, they illegally dealt in 2,981 boxes of smuggled videotapes.

In December 1984, Wang Hengming in Guangzhou, without authorization, placed an order in the name of "Huayi" with Li XX of the Fangcun Company for 3,000 boxes of prohibited videotapes with images, and paid RMB 297,000. Upon learning of this, Li Jincheng, Pan Jialin, and Chen Kunxing all consented to the sale. On January 6, 1985, Li XX chartered an airplane to transport 2,981 boxes of smuggled videotapes to Shanghai. That evening, Chen Kunxing, Wang Hengming, Tao Zhonglin, and others counted the videotapes and together played and watched some of the obscene films among them.

3. In violation of relevant state regulations, they sold 195 imported Suzuki brand motorcycles.

From December 1984 to January 1985, with the consent of Li Jincheng, Chen Kunxing, and Pan Jialin, Wang Hengming, using a fictitious personal name, purchased 203 Suzuki brand motorcycles from He XX of the Shanghai Bicycle Wholesale Department, which were not permitted for wholesale or resale. The illegal turnover was RMB 588,100. They then resold 195 motorcycles to the Fangcun Company, illegally profiting one Toyota brand utility vehicle worth RMB 40,000.

4. They engaged in buying long and selling short, reselling 15,000 woolen blankets.

In November 1984, Wang Hengming, in the name of "Huayi," signed a contract with the Jing'an District Department Store of Shanghai to purchase 35,000 woolen blankets. Immediately thereafter, at a price 12% above the retail price, he resold 15,000 of the blankets on the spot to the Xinyue Trade Company of Haimen County, Jiangsu Province, illegally profiting RMB 105,060.

During the speculation activities, with the consent of Li Jincheng, Pan Jialin, and Chen Kunxing, Wang Hengming, under the guise of "profit sharing," illegally obtained over RMB 73,000 from "Huayi." In the two transactions involving the woolen blankets, under the pretext of receiving "kickbacks," he accepted bribes totaling RMB 25,000. Pan Jialin, taking advantage of his position, accepted bribes from Liu XX of the Guangzhou Wenda Commercial Firm and Li XX of the Fangcun Company: one Jiali brand 14-inch color TV, one Hitachi twin-tub washing machine, one Sanyo stereo cassette recorder, and one Philips heater-fan, collectively valued at over RMB 2,300, for which Pan paid only RMB 380. Chen Kunxing, taking advantage of his position, accepted bribes from Liu XX and Li XX: one Victor brand 14-inch color TV and one Philips heater-fan, collectively valued at over RMB 1,300, for which Chen paid only RMB 590. Tao Zhonglin, taking advantage of his position, accepted a bribe from Liu XX of one Jiali brand color TV valued at over RMB 1,100, for which Tao paid only over RMB 100. In addition to participating in joint criminal activities, in December 1984, Tao Zhonglin, taking advantage of his position, through Wang Hengming, arranged for the Chengnan No. 3 Warehouse in Liyang County, Jiangsu Province to purchase 29,640 woolen blankets from the Jing'an District Department Store of Shanghai on a black-market basis. Under the guise of receiving a "kickback," Tao accepted a bribe of RMB 50,000. In January 1985, Tao Zhonglin acted as an intermediary in the resale of 200 Sony brand 14-inch remote control color TVs, valued at a total of RMB 240,000, between Li XX of the Guangzhou Fangcun Company and Wu X of the Jiangdong Industrial and Economic Corporation of Ningbo City, Zhejiang Province, from which Tao profited RMB 3,000.

In addition, in early November 1984, "Huayi" had an economic dispute with the Zunyi Ferroalloy Labor Service Company of Guizhou. The defendants Li Jincheng and Pan Jialin actually used the powers of the public security organs, employing a summons from the Putuo Branch and dispatching a patrol car, to illegally detain the other party's procurement personnel by summons.

On January 21, 1986, the Shanghai Intermediate People's Court rendered its judgment at first instance, finding:

Defendant Li Jincheng, as Deputy Director of the Public Security Bureau and in charge of supervising "Huayi," consented to the sale of goods not freely tradable under state regulations. The illegal turnover was particularly huge. Although he did not line his own pockets, he bears supervisory responsibility for the speculative activities of "Huayi" and is guilty of the crime of speculation and should be punished.

Defendant Pan Jialin, as a public security cadre and General Manager of "Huayi," misappropriated customs case-handling funds during the operation of "Huayi," consented to the sale of goods not freely tradable under state regulations, with an illegally large turnover. He also abused his police authority by illegally using public security documents to transport imported video recorders from Guangzhou. He bears supervisory and direct responsibility for the speculative activities of "Huayi." Additionally, he took advantage of his position to accept bribes. He is guilty of the crimes of speculation and bribery and should be punished.

Defendant Chen Kunxing, as Deputy Director of the Anti-Smuggling Division and Captain of the Anti-Smuggling Team of Customs, during the operation of "Huayi," consented to the sale of goods not freely tradable under state regulations, with a particularly huge illegal turnover. He bears supervisory responsibility for the speculative activities of "Huayi" and, taking advantage of his position, accepted bribes. He is guilty of the crimes of speculation and bribery and should be punished.

Defendant Tao Zhonglin, as a public security cadre and Deputy General Manager of "Huayi," during the operation of "Huayi," sold goods not freely tradable under state regulations, with a particularly huge illegal turnover. Moreover, during the speculative activities, he abused police authority by illegally using public security documents. He is a person directly responsible for the speculative activities of "Huayi." Tao Zhonglin also individually conspired with others to engage in speculative activities and, taking advantage of his position, accepted bribes, with a huge amount and particularly serious circumstances. He is guilty of the crimes of speculation and bribery and should be punished. Given that Tao Zhonglin had a good attitude in confessing after being brought to justice, a lighter punishment may be imposed as appropriate.

Defendant Wang Hengming, during his employment with "Huayi," fraudulently using the names of the public security and customs authorities, unauthorizedly trafficked in smuggled videotapes, took the lead in selling imported motorcycles, cassette recorders, and other goods not freely tradable under state regulations, engaged in speculation (buying long and selling short) and resold woolen blankets, with a particularly huge illegal turnover. He personally derived huge illegal profits from these activities. He is a person directly responsible for the speculative activities of "Huayi," with particularly serious circumstances. Wang also took advantage of his employment to accept bribes, with a huge amount. He is guilty of the crimes of speculation and bribery and should be severely punished. Given that Wang Hengming engaged in reporting and accusing after being brought to justice, a lighter punishment may be imposed as appropriate.

In accordance with Article 118, Article 185, Article 64, Article 60, and Paragraph 1 of Article 53 of the Criminal Law, and Subparagraphs (1) and (2) of Paragraph 1 of Article 1 of the Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Severely Punishing Criminals Who Seriously Sabotage the Economy, in comparison with Article 155 of the Criminal Law, the court sentenced Li Jincheng to five years' imprisonment for the crime of speculation; sentenced Pan Jialin to five years' imprisonment for the crime of speculation and two years' imprisonment for the crime of bribery, with the combined execution term being seven years' imprisonment; sentenced Chen Kunxing to four years' imprisonment for the crime of speculation and one year's imprisonment for the crime of bribery, with the combined execution term being five years' imprisonment; sentenced Tao Zhonglin to life imprisonment for the crimes of speculation and bribery, with deprivation of political rights for life; and sentenced Wang Hengming to life imprisonment for the crimes of speculation and bribery, with deprivation of political rights for life. The illicit money and goods were to be recovered. Chen Kunxing appealed on the grounds that he had not agreed to "Huayi" dealing in smuggled videotapes and Suzuki motorcycles, and Tao Zhonglin appealed on the grounds that he requested leniency.

Upon investigation by the Shanghai High People's Court, regarding "Huayi"'s dealing in smuggled videotapes, Chen Kunxing, together with Li Jincheng and Pan Jialin, had heard Wang Hengming's report and raised no objections. After the videotapes were shipped to Shanghai, Chen Kunxing participated in counting them and played and watched some of the obscene films among them. In early December 1984, when Wang Hengming, representing "Huayi," was negotiating a contract with others to purchase motorcycles, Chen Kunxing was not only present but also asked the other party to "give more help." Therefore, Chen Kunxing's grounds for appeal were untenable. Tao Zhonglin's appeal requesting leniency lacked sufficient justification. On February 19, 1986, the second instance court ruled to reject the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

On March 3, 1986, at the 246th Session of the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, pursuant to Paragraph 1 of Article 11 of the Organic Law of the People's Courts of the People's Republic of China, when summarizing trial experience, it was held that the convictions and sentences imposed by the Shanghai High and Intermediate People's Courts on each defendant in this case were correct. Although Li Jincheng in this case did not line his own pockets, he bore supervisory responsibility for the speculative activities of "Huayi" and must be punished according to law.
